/-- Add one empty first stage to a representation of a conditionally linear
function. -/
private def CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1) :=
  .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => t)

@[simp]
private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) (x : ι → K) :
    CondLinearTerm.eval t.raiseLevel x = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
  simp [CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval]

private theorem CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t.raiseLevel S := by
  exact ⟨Finset.empty_subset S, fun _ => by simpa using ht⟩

/-- Raise a representation of a conditionally linear function by a specified
number of empty stages. -/
private def CondLinearTerm.raiseBy {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    (d : ℕ) → {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell →
      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + d)
  | 0, _, t => t
  | d + 1, _, t => (raiseBy d t).raiseLevel

@[simp]
private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseBy {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ℕ) {ell : ℕ}
    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) (x : ι → K) :
    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.raiseBy d t) x = CondLinearTerm.eval t x := by
  induction d with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ d ih => simp [CondLinearTerm.raiseBy, ih]

private theorem CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (d : ℕ) {ell : ℕ}
    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S : Finset ι}
    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.raiseBy d t) S := by
  induction d with
  | zero => exact ht
  | succ d ih => exact CondLinearTerm.raiseLevel_supportedOn ih

/-- Conditional linearity is monotone in the number of levels. -/
private theorem IsCondLinearOn.mono_level {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell k : ℕ}
    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    (h : ell ≤ k) : IsCondLinearOn K S k L := by
  rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩

(⟨((ell + 1) + 1) - 1, Nat.sub_lt h (by decide)⟩ : Fin ((ell + 1) + 1)) =
          last.succ := by
      apply Fin.ext
      simp [last]
    funext x
    rw [hlast, clDataConsMarginal_succ]
    rw [congrFun ((d (clDataFirst S₁ L₁ x)).top hTail) x]
    rfl

/-- Every positive-level supported representation of a conditionally linear
function admits support-relative prefix decomposition data. -/
private theorem CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} (hEll : 1 ≤ ell)
    (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) {S : Finset ι}
    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
    Nonempty (CLDataOn K ι S ell (CondLinearTerm.eval t)) := by
  induction ell using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing S with
  | h ell ih =>
      cases ell with
      | zero => omega
      | succ n =>
          cases n with
          | zero => exact CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_one t ht
          | succ n =>
              cases t with
              | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
                  apply CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn_succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ht
                  intro y
                  exact ih (n + 1) (by omega) (by omega) (rest y) (ht.2 y)

/-- A map is `ell`-level conditionally linear exactly when it admits the
prefix decomposition of `lem:cl-kth`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1206-1226`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-262`. -/
theorem isCondLinear_iff_nonempty_clData {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ} (hEll : 1 ≤ ell)
    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
    IsCondLinear ell L ↔ Nonempty (CLData K ι ell L) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
    rw [← ht_eval]
    obtain ⟨d⟩ := CondLinearTerm.nonempty_clDataOn hEll t ht
    exact ⟨{
      marginal := d.marginal
      factor := d.factor
      linear := d.linear
      marginal_cl := d.marginal_cl
      factor_disjoint := d.factor_disjoint
      factor_cover := fun x a => d.factor_cover x a (Finset.mem_univ a)
      linear_supported := d.linear_supported
      sum_formula := d.sum_formula
      top := d.top
    }⟩
  · rintro ⟨d⟩
    have hPos : 0 < ell := by omega
    let last : Fin ell := ⟨ell - 1, Nat.sub_lt hPos (by decide)⟩
    have hLast := d.marginal_cl last
    rw [d.top hPos] at hLast
    simpa only [IsCondLinear, last, Nat.sub_add_cancel hEll] using hLast

/-- Conditional linearity is monotone in the number of levels. -/
private theorem IsCondLinearOn.mono_level {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell k : ℕ}
    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    (h : ell ≤ k) : IsCondLinearOn K S k L := by
  rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
  have hk : ell + (k - ell) = k := Nat.add_sub_of_le h
  rw [← hk]
  exact ⟨CondLinearTerm.raiseBy (k - ell) t,
    CondLinearTerm.raiseBy_supportedOn _ ht,
    funext fun x => by rw [CondLinearTerm.eval_raiseBy, congrFun ht_eval x]⟩

/-- A conditionally-linear map supported on `S` has values supported on `S`. -/
private theorem IsCondLinearOn.apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
    {L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)} (hL : IsCondLinearOn K S ell L)
    (x : ι → K) {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ S) : L x a = 0 := by
  rcases hL with ⟨t, ht, ht_eval⟩
  rw [← congrFun (congrFun ht_eval x) a]
  exact CondLinearTerm.eval_eq_zero_of_not_mem ht x ha

auxiliary uses `0` for the empty family; `lem:cl-func-prod` separately assumes

def directSumLevel {m : ℕ} (ell : Fin m → ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.sup ell

/-- Direct sums over a register partition preserve conditional linearity. The
level-zero case is included explicitly, as required by the local correction to
`lem:cl-func-prod`; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1255-1266`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`. -/
theorem IsCondLinear.directSum {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m)
    (V : Fin m → Finset ι) (ell : Fin m → ℕ)
    (L : Fin m → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
    (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ i, a ∈ V i)
    (hL : ∀ j, IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (ell j) (L j)) :
    IsCondLinear (directSumLevel ell) (condLinearDirectSum V L) := by
  classical
  let _sourceIndex : Fin m := ⟨0, hm⟩
  have hLevel (j : Fin m) : ell j ≤ directSumLevel ell :=
    Finset.le_sup (f := ell) (Finset.mem_univ j)
  have hRaised (j : Fin m) :
      IsCondLinearOn K (V j) (directSumLevel ell) (L j) :=
    IsCondLinearOn.mono_level (hL j) (hLevel j)
  have hUnion : Finset.univ.biUnion V = (Finset.univ : Finset ι) := by
    apply Finset.eq_univ_of_forall
    intro a
    obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨j, Finset.mem_univ _, haj⟩
  have hSum := IsCondLinearOn.directSum_sameLevel V (directSumLevel ell) L
    hDisjoint hRaised
  rw [hUnion] at hSum
  exact hSum

I’ll leave the Pauli family as an explicitly source-faithful tracked obligation unless the existing coordinate infrastructure makes its proof reasonably local.

import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.Distribution

/-! # Operations on finite distributions

Products, convex mixtures, dependent binds, and normalized restrictions used by
the QPBT distributions, together with the generic push-forward calculus for
finite and uniform distributions. Their source uses occur in the line-point
sampler, typed conditionally linear distributions, sandwich products, and
restricted line distributions cited below.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- The product of two finite distributions, a formalization-only auxiliary
used by the sandwich construction; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-480`,
paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. -/
noncomputable def Distribution.prod {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) : Distribution (α × β) where
  support := μ.support.product ν.support
  weight p := μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
  nonnegative p := mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative p.1) (ν.nonnegative p.2)
  outsideSupport p hp := by
    by_cases hμ : p.1 ∈ μ.support
    · have hν : p.2 ∉ ν.support := by
        intro h
        exact hp (Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hμ, h⟩)
      simp [ν.outsideSupport p.2 hν]
    · simp [μ.outsideSupport p.1 hμ]

/-- The product of two probability distributions is a probability
distribution; blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:454-480`, paper
`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`. -/
theorem Distribution.prod_isProbability {α β : Type*}
    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
    (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hν : ν.IsProbability) :
    (Distribution.prod μ ν).IsProbability := by
  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    Distribution.prod]
  calc
    (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support, μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) =
        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, ∑ b ∈ ν.support, μ.weight a * ν.weight b := by
      exact Finset.sum_product' μ.support ν.support
        (fun a b => μ.weight a * ν.weight b)
    _ =
        ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * ∑ b ∈ ν.support, ν.weight b := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      exact (Finset.mul_sum ν.support (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm
    _ = ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a := by
      rw [hν.weight_sum_eq_one]
      simp
    _ = 1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one

/-- The convex mixture with a coefficient in `[0,1]`, as used for
the equal mixture in `def:line-point-dist`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:125-135`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
noncomputable def Distribution.mix {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (t : ℝ) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    (μ ν : Distribution α) : Distribution α where
  support := μ.support ∪ ν.support
  weight a := t * μ.weight a + (1 - t) * ν.weight a
  nonnegative a := by
    exact add_nonneg
      (mul_nonneg ht0 (μ.nonnegative a))
      (mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr ht1) (ν.nonnegative a))
  outsideSupport a ha := by
    have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_left _ h)
    have hν : a ∉ ν.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_union_right _ h)
    simp [μ.outsideSupport a hμ, ν.outsideSupport a hν]

/-- A convex mixture of probability distributions is a probability distribution;
`def:line-point-dist`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:125-135`, paper
`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
theorem Distribution.mix_isProbability {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (t : ℝ) (μ ν : Distribution α) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
    (hν : ν.IsProbability) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) :
    (Distribution.mix t ht0 ht1 μ ν).IsProbability := by
  have hμ_union :
      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, μ.weight a = 1 := by
    apply hμ.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
    intro a ha
    exact Finset.mem_union_left ν.support ha
  have hν_union :
      ∑ a ∈ μ.support ∪ ν.support, ν.weight a = 1 := by
    apply hν.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
    intro a ha
    exact Finset.mem_union_right μ.support ha
  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    Distribution.mix]
  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.mul_sum,
    hμ_union, hν_union]
  ring

/-- The dependent bind of finite distributions used for typed question
distributions, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1400-1404`, paper
`07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
noncomputable def Distribution.bind {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) : Distribution β where
  support := μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support)
  weight b := ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b
  nonnegative b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => mul_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) ((ν a).nonnegative b)
  outsideSupport b hb := by
    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    intro a ha
    have hnot : b ∉ (ν a).support := by
      intro h
      exact hb (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, h⟩)
    simp [ν a |>.outsideSupport b hnot]

/-- A dependent bind of probability distributions is a probability distribution;
blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1400-1404`, paper `07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
theorem Distribution.bind_isProbability {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution β) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
    (hν : ∀ a ∈ μ.support, (ν a).IsProbability) :
    (Distribution.bind μ ν).IsProbability := by
  classical
  have hν_union (a : α) (ha : a ∈ μ.support) :
      ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support), (ν a).weight b = 1 := by
    apply (hν a ha).weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset
    intro b hb
    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨a, ha, hb⟩
  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    Distribution.bind]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  calc
    (∑ a ∈ μ.support,
        ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
          μ.weight a * (ν a).weight b) =
        ∑ a ∈ μ.support,
          μ.weight a *
            ∑ b ∈ μ.support.biUnion (fun a => (ν a).support),
              (ν a).weight b := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      exact (Finset.mul_sum _ (fun b => (ν a).weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm
    _ = ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a ha
      rw [hν_union a ha]
      simp
    _ = 1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one

/-- Restrict a distribution to a decidable positive-mass event and normalize it,
as in `def:ith-restricted-line`; blueprint
`ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:600-618`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
noncomputable def Distribution.restrict {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (μ : Distribution α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    (hpos : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) : Distribution α where
  support := μ.support.filter p
  weight a := if p a then μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b else 0
  nonnegative a := by
    split
    · exact div_nonneg (μ.nonnegative a) (le_of_lt hpos)
    · exact le_rfl
  outsideSupport a ha := by
    by_cases hp : p a
    · have hμ : a ∉ μ.support := fun h => ha (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨h, hp⟩)
      simp [hp, μ.outsideSupport a hμ]
    · simp [hp]

/-- Restriction to a positive-mass event preserves total probability;
`def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint
`ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:600-618`, paper
`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1038-1048`. -/
theorem Distribution.restrict_isProbability {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (μ : Distribution α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    (hpos : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) :
    (Distribution.restrict μ p hpos).IsProbability := by
  simp only [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight,
    Distribution.restrict]
  calc
    (∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p,
        if p a then μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b else 0) =
        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p,
          μ.weight a / ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a ha
      rw [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
    _ = (∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a) /
        ∑ b ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight b := by
      rw [Finset.sum_div]
    _ = 1 := div_self hpos.ne'

/-! ### Push-forwards of finite and uniform distributions

The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
linear distributions rely on.
-/

/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
`Distribution`. -/
theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
    μ = ν := by
  cases μ with
  | mk s w hn ho =>
    cases ν with
    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
      have hw : w = w' := hweight
      subst hs
      subst hw
      rfl

/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
    rw [Finset.image_image]
    rfl
  · funext c
    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
      intro a ha
      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
    rw [← hkey]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
    congr 1
    ext a
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩

/-- Every point of a finite type carries the same uniform weight.
Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α : Type*)
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
  simp [uniformDistribution]

/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform
distribution forward to the uniform distribution.  Formalization-only
auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]

    15	The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

 \begin{definition}[Conditionally linear distributions]\label{def:cl-dist}
 	\uses{def:cl-func}
 	Let $L, R \colon V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions. The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,R)$} is the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$ for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.

 	\begin{enumerate}
 		\item[(i)] for each $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, \ell\}$, a function $L_{\le k} \colon V \to V$, called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
 		\item[(ii)] for each $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{<k}(V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\,u}$ of $V$, called the \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
 		\item[(iii)] for each $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{<k}(V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\,u} \colon V_{k,\,u} \to V_{k,\,u}$, called the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
 	\end{enumerate}

 	\begin{enumerate}
 		\item $L_{\le k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;

 		\item $L_{\le k}(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,x^{L_{<i}}}$;
 		\item $L = L_{\le \ell}$.

 \section{Typed conditionally linear distributions}
 % Paper section label sec:types kept for cross-reference fidelity. Only the mathematical
 % typed material (typed CL functions and distributions, graph distributions) is stated
 % here; the typed sampler and verifier machinery of the source is outside the scope of
 % the mathematical development.
 \label{sec:types}
 
 The question distribution of the Pauli basis test is \emph{typed}: each question is a pair consisting of a type, drawn together with the other player's type from the edges of a fixed \emph{type graph}, and a question content, drawn from a CL distribution determined by the pair of types.
 
 \begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]\label{def:typed-cl-functions}
 	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsTypedCondLinearFamily}
 	\leanok
 	\uses{def:cl-func}
 	Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite set (the \emph{type set}) and let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \ge 0$. A \emph{$\mathcal T$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_t\}_{t \in \mathcal T}$ such that, for each $t \in \mathcal T$, $L_t$ is an $\ell$-level conditionally linear function on $V$.
 \end{definition}
 
 % Nonemptiness of the edge set is stated explicitly here: with E empty, m = k = 0 and the
 % normalization 1/(2m-k) below is undefined. The source
 % (references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82) leaves this boundary hypothesis implicit.
 \begin{definition}[Graph distribution]\label{def:graph-distribution}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.graphDistribution}
+	\leanok
 	Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and nonempty edge set $E$. Edges in $E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u = v$ represents a self-loop. Suppose there are $m \ge 1$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops. Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of $G$} is the distribution over $U \times U$ such that for every $(u,v) \in U \times U$,
 	\[
 		\mu_G(u, v) =
 		\begin{cases}
 			1/(2m-k) & \text{if } \{u,v\} \in E\,,\\
 			0 & \text{otherwise}\,.
 		\end{cases}
 	\]
 	This is identical to the uniform distribution over ordered pairs $(u,v) \in U \times U$ such that $\{u,v\} \in E$: each edge that is not a self-loop contributes two ordered pairs, and each self-loop contributes one, whence the normalization $2m-k$.
 \end{definition}
 
+\begin{lemma}[Total mass of the graph distribution]\label{lem:graph-distribution-mass}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.graphDistribution_isProbability}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{def:graph-distribution}
+	Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with nonempty edge set $E$. Then the graph distribution $\mu_G$ of Definition~\ref{def:graph-distribution} has total mass one, that is, $\sum_{(u,v) \in U \times U} \mu_G(u,v) = 1$.
+\end{lemma}
+\begin{proof}
+	\leanok
+	\uses{def:graph-distribution}
+	The distribution $\mu_G$ is uniform on the set of ordered pairs $(u,v) \in U \times U$ with $\{u,v\} \in E$, and that set is nonempty because $E$ is: an edge $\{u,v\} \in E$ yields the ordered pair $(u,v)$. A uniform distribution on a nonempty finite set has total mass one.
+\end{proof}

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary equivalence splitting an ambient low-degree
+vector into its point, seed, and direction blocks. -/
+private def ldSpaceSplit (L : LdParams) :
+    LdSpace L ≃ ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) where
+  toFun z := ((LdSpace.point z, LdSpace.seed z), LdSpace.direction z)
+  invFun p := fun i =>
+    match i with
+    | .inl (.inl j) => p.1.1 j
+    | .inl (.inr _) => p.1.2
+    | .inr j => p.2 j
+  left_inv z := by
+    funext i
+    rcases i with (j | u) | j
+    · rfl
+    · cases u
+      rfl
+    · rfl
+  right_inv p := by
+    obtain ⟨⟨a, b⟩, c⟩ := p
+    rfl
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point block of a uniformly random
+ambient vector is uniform. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_point (L : LdParams) :
+    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point =
+      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
+  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
+      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
+    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
+  calc
+    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point
+        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
+            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
+          rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
+          rfl
+    _ = ((uniformDistribution
+          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
+            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by rw [hsplit]
+    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
+          rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]
+    _ = uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := uniformDistribution_map_fst
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the shared scalar coordinate of a
+uniformly random ambient vector is uniform. -/
+private theorem map_uniformDistribution_seed (L : LdParams) :
+    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed =
+      uniformDistribution (ScalarQ L) := by
+  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
+      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=

   131	# sanitize_to <src> <dest> <max-lines> — control-char strip, fence breaking,
   132	# truncation (DESIGN.md invariant 6).  dispatch.sh sanitizes attachments again;
   133	# this is the copy that also protects the no-dispatcher fallback path.
   134	sanitize_to() {
   135	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" <<'PY'
   136	import sys
   137	src, dest, max_lines = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
   138	try:
   139	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   140	except OSError:
   141	    raw = ""
   142	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
   143	keep = []
   144	for ch in raw:
   145	    o = ord(ch)
   146	    if ch in "\n\t" or (32 <= o < 127) or o > 159:
   147	        keep.append(ch)
   148	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")
   149	truncated = 0
   150	if len(lines) > max_lines:
   151	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   152	    lines = lines[:max_lines]
   153	out = []
   154	for line in lines:
   155	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   156	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   157	        line = " " + line
   158	    out.append(line)

   160	    out.append("... [%d further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"
   161	               % truncated)
   162	open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")

   166	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   167	# Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
   168	# re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
   169	acquire_lock() {
   170	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   171	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   172	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   173	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   174	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   175	      warn "removing stale lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
   176	      rm -rf "$dir"
   177	      continue
   178	    fi
   179	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   180	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
   181	    fi
   182	    [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
   183	    sleep 5
   184	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   185	  done
   186	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   187	  printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   188	  LOCK_HELD="$dir"
   189	}

   211	# resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
   212	# registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.  Creates it if the
   213	# branch has no worktree yet.
   214	resolve_worktree() {
   215	  local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   216	  found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
   217	    awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
   218	      /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}
   219	      $0 == "branch " b {print p; exit}')"
   220	  if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
   221	    printf '%s\n' "$found"
   222	    return 0
   223	  fi
   224	  safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   225	  dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   226	  if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
   227	    have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
   228	    if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
   229	      printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   230	      return 0
   231	    fi
   232	    die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
   233	  fi
   234	  mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   235	  git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||
   236	    die "git worktree add $dest $branch failed"
   237	  if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then
   238	    "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" "$dest" >&2 ||
   239	      warn "worktree-setup.sh failed for $dest; the reviewer runs without a warmed build cache"
   240	  else
   241	    warn "local/bin/worktree-setup.sh not found; the reviewer worktree has no warmed Lean build cache (local/protocols/build-cache.md)"
   242	  fi
   243	  printf '%s\n' "$dest"
   244	}

   246	# run_agent <role> <sandbox> <worktree> <persona-path> <task-file>
   247	#           <standalone-prompt> <context-file> <out-file> <model>
   248	#
   249	# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh when it exists, so the
   250	# session lands in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (DESIGN.md, "Agent
   251	# sessions").  The fallback is a direct codex exec with a loud warning.
   252	run_agent() {
   253	  local role="$1" sandbox="$2" wt="$3" persona="$4" taskfile="$5"
   254	  local standalone="$6" ctx="$7" out="$8" model="$9"
   255	  local dlog="$out.dispatch.log" task_text last rc=0

   271	    # observed on PR #0003, events.md 2026-08-31), so retrying cannot
   272	    # duplicate a review.
   273	    local attempt started ended tokens
   274	    for attempt in 1 2; do
   275	      started="$(date +%s)"
   276	      set +e
   277	      if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   278	        MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL="$model" \
   279	          "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   280	      else
   281	        MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   282	      fi

   284	      set -e
   285	      ended="$(date +%s)"
   286	      tokens="$(sed -n 's/^tokens_total: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"

   302	    fi

   304	  fi

   306	  warn "local/bin/dispatch.sh not found; falling back to a direct 'codex exec'. This session will NOT appear in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl."

   308	    die "codex CLI not found on PATH and no local/bin/dispatch.sh to delegate to"

   312	      -m "$model" -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"

   314	    MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 codex exec --sandbox "$sandbox" -C "$wt" \
   315	      -o "$out" -- "$(cat "$standalone")" >"$dlog"
   316	  fi
   317	  rc=$?
   318	  set -e

Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Issue titles, slugs, and branch\n  names stay bracket-free.\n\n## Practical Defaults for Agents\n\nWhen editing Lean code:\n\n1. Read the paper source\n2. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Issue titles, slugs, and branch\n  names stay bracket-free.\n\n## Practical Defaults for Agents\n\nWhen editing Lean code:\n\n1. Read the paper source\n2.
